title: Nutrition in animals
status: draft: written 18 Nov 2026 offline for Grade 9 Integrated Science; not yet checked by a CBC Integrated Science teacher; not loaded by the live tutor
notes: Use skulls or pictures of a goat, a dog and a human for dentition, the learner's own teeth in a mirror, and a chart of the digestive system. Chewing bread until it tastes sweet shows digestion starting in the mouth.

skills.key_step: The child names modes of nutrition in animals (herbivores, carnivores, omnivores, and parasites) and classifies animals by their diet and dentition.

floor.question: Which group does a goat belong to?

representations: a sorting table: herbivore, carnivore, omnivore, parasite
steps: Parasites: feed on a living host (tick, tapeworm).

board.do: Draw four columns: herbivore, carnivore, omnivore, parasite.
Write goat, lion, person, tick below.

board.say: Which column does it go in?

board.do: Ask the child to sort the rest.

misconceptions.ask: Where does a tick get its food?
misconceptions.repair: Parasites feed on a living host.

checks.question: Give an example of an omnivore.

skills.key_step: The child names incisors (cut), canines (tear), premolars and molars (grind), describes their shape and links dentition to diet (big canines in carnivores, broad molars in herbivores).

floor.question: What do teeth do to food?

board.do: Draw a row of teeth: chisel, point, broad.
Ask the child to label the other two.

misconceptions.ask: Which teeth are long and pointed?
Which teeth are broad and at the back?
What food does a goat eat?

checks.question: Why do carnivores have large canines?

skills.key_step: The child describes where digestion happens in a human (mouth: saliva begins starch; stomach: protein begins; small intestine: completed and absorbed; large intestine: water absorbed) in order.

floor.prerequisite: Knows the order of the digestive parts.
floor.question: What comes after the stomach?

representations: a chart of the digestive system
a flow chart: part, what happens
steps: Mouth: chewing and saliva start on starch.
Stomach: acid and juices start on protein.
Small intestine: digestion finished; food absorbed into blood.
Large intestine: water absorbed; waste leaves.

board.do: Draw the path from the mouth to the anus.

board.say: What happens to digested food here?

board.do: Wait for "it is absorbed into the blood".
Ask the child to write what happens in the mouth and stomach.

misconceptions.ask: Why does bread taste sweet after long chewing?
Where does food pass into the blood?
misconceptions.repair: Absorption is in the small intestine.

listen_for: water is absorbed in the oesophagus
misconceptions.ask: Which part takes in water from waste?

checks.question: Where does the digestion of starch begin?
